title: Is Your Water Older Than the SUN? 💧
description:
Quick: what's older, the Sun or the water you drink? Some of the water. The Sun is about 4.6 billion years old, but scientists think up to half of the water in Earth's oceans (and so in your glass, and in you) first formed as ice in the freezing, dark cloud of gas and dust the Sun was born from, at around -260 °C. How do we know? Heavy water. A tiny share of water carries a heavier kind of hydrogen, and Earth's water has more of it than the young Sun's disk of gas could have made: only the deep cold of that cloud makes water that heavy. And you're mostly water, so bits of you are older than the Sun. What did you guess: Sun or water?

Source: Cleeves et al., "The ancient heritage of water ice in the solar system", Science, 2014 (30 to 50 % of Earth's ocean water older than the Sun, by their model).

Bonus: about 1 in every 6,400 hydrogen atoms in seawater is the heavy kind.
